   198|### The Garage Stays Open
   199|
   200|High school brought new interests. New demands. New distractions. I still spent time in the garage, but less of it.    201|
   202|Years later, when I had my own children, I tried to recreate this magic. I built a workbench in my own garage. Bought tools and lumber and plans.    203|
   204|Bob sometimes wonders what his father felt, whether he knew, in some wordless way, that we were building more than toy airplanes.    208|The skills learned in that garage—the patience to measure twice, the courage to fail and rebuild, the understanding that invisible forces could be harnessed to do extraordinary things—would soon find an outlet far beyond anything Bob could have imagined.
